items.title: Sid Davilla Interview, 1969-04-17
items.q: The interviewee addresses 'Tom' directly multiple times (e.g., '...trend the last ten years, Tom.', 'No, not at all, Tom.'), indicating familiarity, but no specific professional or personal relationship (like friend, mentor, or collaborator) is described in the text.

ctx.x: Jim Roberts. Well, let me ask you now about, um, um, it seems to me that in the last, I don't know, ten years, or maybe more than ten years, there's been quite a big change on Bourbon Street in terms of the kind of entertainment that's provided, and this has been presumable dictated by financial considerations and so on. Um, would you like to discuss this a little bit and the sort of change that has taken place on the street?

Well, let's see, now, first, I guess I've been on Bourbon Street about half of my life. Twenty-five years, twenty-six years altogether. And, uh, it's become more of a midway now. There's a lot of lookers and a lot of, uh, walkers, and, uh, actually the people don't go into clubs, or, and this has been the trend the last ten years, Tom. They don't go into these clubs as they used to. There'd be about sixteen girly, girly clubs, so-called strip clubs on the street. And there were three jazz places, as I mentioned,…
Were there sixteen strip places at that time?
